43: impl TryFrom<&str> for FormatSummary {
44:     type Error = FormatParseError;
45: 
46:     fn try_from(literal: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
47:         let format_string = FormatString::from_str(literal)?;
48: 
49:         let mut autos = Vec::new();
50:         let mut indices = Vec::new();
51:         let mut keywords = Vec::new();
52:         let mut has_nested_parts = false;
53: 
54:         for format_part in &format_string.format_parts {
55:             let FormatPart::Field {
56:                 field_name,
57:                 format_spec,
58:                 ..
59:             } = format_part
60:             else {
61:                 continue;
62:             };
63:             let parsed = FieldName::parse(field_name)?;
64:             match parsed.field_type {
65:                 FieldType::Auto => autos.push(autos.len()),
66:                 FieldType::Index(i) => indices.push(i),
67:                 FieldType::Keyword(k) => keywords.push(Name::from(k)),
68:             };
69: 
70:             let nested = FormatString::from_str(format_spec)?;
71:             for nested_part in nested.format_parts {
72:                 let FormatPart::Field { field_name, .. } = nested_part else {
73:                     continue;
74:                 };
75:                 let parsed = FieldName::parse(&field_name)?;
76:                 match parsed.field_type {
77:                     FieldType::Auto => autos.push(autos.len()),
78:                     FieldType::Index(i) => indices.push(i),
79:                     FieldType::Keyword(k) => keywords.push(Name::from(k)),
80:                 };
81:                 has_nested_parts = true;
82:             }
83:         }
84: 
85:         Ok(FormatSummary {
86:             autos,
87:             indices,
88:             keywords,
89:             has_nested_parts,
90:         })
91:     }

94: impl FormatSummary {
95:     /// Generate a [`Edit`] to remove unused positional arguments from a `format` call.
96:     pub(crate) fn remove_unused_positional_arguments_from_format_call(
97:         &self,
98:         unused_arguments: &[usize],
99:         call: &ast::ExprCall,
100:         locator: &Locator,
101:         stylist: &Stylist,
102:     ) -> Result<Edit> {
103:         let ast::ExprCall {
104:             func,
105:             arguments,
106:             range: call_range,
107:         } = call;
108: 
109:         let named_arguments_are_keepable = arguments.keywords.iter().all(|keyword| {
110:             let has_value = !locator.slice(&keyword.value).is_empty();
111:             match &keyword.arg {
112:                 Some(name) => has_value && !name.as_str().is_empty(),
113:                 None => has_value,
114:             }
115:         });
116:         let unused_arguments: Vec<usize> = unused_arguments
117:             .iter()
118:             .copied()
119:             .filter(|index| {
120:                 named_arguments_are_keepable
121:                     && *index < arguments.args.len() + arguments.keywords.len()
122:                     && !self.indices.contains(index)
123:             })
124:             .collect();
125: 
126:         let source_range = TextRange::new(func.start().min(call_range.start()), call_range.end());
127:         let source_code = locator.slice(source_range);
128:         let wrapped = format!("({source_code})");
129:         let mut expression = match_expression(&wrapped)?;
130:         {
131:             let cst_call = match_call_mut(&mut expression)?;
132:             let mut index = 0;
133:             cst_call.args.retain(|_| {
134:                 let is_unused = unused_arguments.contains(&index);
135:                 index += 1;
136:                 !is_unused
137:             });
138:         }
139: 
140:         let mut state = CodegenState {
141:             default_newline: stylist.line_ending().as_str(),
142:             default_indent: stylist.indentation(),
143:             ..Default::default()
144:         };
145:         expression.codegen(&mut state);
146:         let mut output = state.to_string();
147:         output.drain(0..1);
148:         output.drain(output.len() - 1..output.len());
149:         Ok(Edit::range_replacement(output, *call_range))
150:     }
151: }

13: /// Generate a [`Edit`] to remove unused keys from format dict.
14: pub(super) fn remove_unused_format_arguments_from_dict(
15:     unused_arguments: &[usize],
16:     dict: &ast::ExprDict,
17:     locator: &Locator,
18:     stylist: &Stylist,
19: ) -> Result<Edit> {
20:     let source_code = locator.slice(dict);
21:     transform_expression(source_code, stylist, |mut expression| {
22:         let dict = match_dict(&mut expression)?;
23: 
24:         // Remove the elements at the given indexes.
25:         let mut index = 0;
26:         dict.elements.retain(|_| {
27:             let is_unused = unused_arguments.contains(&index);
28:             index += 1;
29:             !is_unused
30:         });
31: 
32:         Ok(expression)
33:     })
34:     .map(|output| Edit::range_replacement(output, dict.range()))
35: }
36: 
37: /// Generate a [`Edit`] to remove unused keyword arguments from a `format` call.
38: pub(super) fn remove_unused_keyword_arguments_from_format_call(
39:     unused_arguments: &[usize],
40:     call: &ast::ExprCall,
41:     locator: &Locator,
42:     stylist: &Stylist,
43: ) -> Result<Edit> {
44:     let source_code = locator.slice(call);
45:     transform_expression(source_code, stylist, |mut expression| {
46:         let call = match_call_mut(&mut expression)?;
47: 
48:         // Remove the keyword arguments at the given indexes.
49:         let mut index = 0;
50:         call.args.retain(|arg| {
51:             if arg.keyword.is_none() {
52:                 return true;
53:             }
54: 
55:             let is_unused = unused_arguments.contains(&index);
56:             index += 1;
57:             !is_unused
58:         });
59: 
60:         Ok(expression)
61:     })
62:     .map(|output| Edit::range_replacement(output, call.range()))
63: }

65: /// Generate a [`Edit`] to remove the binding from an exception handler.
66: pub(crate) fn remove_exception_handler_assignment(
67:     bound_exception: &Binding,
68:     locator: &Locator,
69: ) -> Result<Edit> {
70:     // Find the position just after the exception name. This is a late pass so we only have the
71:     // binding and can't look its parent in the AST up anymore.
72:     // ```
73:     // except ZeroDivisionError as err:
74:     //                             ^^^ This is the bound_exception range
75:     //                         ^^^^ lex this range
76:     //                         ^ preceding_end (we want to remove from here)
77:     // ```
78:     // There can't be any comments in that range.
79:     let mut tokenizer =
80:         BackwardsTokenizer::up_to(bound_exception.start(), locator.contents(), &[]).skip_trivia();
81: 
82:     // Eat the `as` token.
83:     let preceding = tokenizer
84:         .next()
85:         .context("expected the exception name to be preceded by `as`")?;
86:     debug_assert!(matches!(preceding.kind, SimpleTokenKind::As));

88:     // Lex to the end of the preceding token, which should be the exception value.
89:     let preceding = tokenizer
90:         .next()
91:         .context("expected the exception name to be preceded by a token")?;
92: 
93:     // Lex forwards, to the `:` token.
94:     let following = SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(bound_exception.end(), locator.contents())
95:         .skip_trivia()
96:         .next()
97:         .context("expected the exception name to be followed by a colon")?;
98:     debug_assert!(matches!(following.kind, SimpleTokenKind::Colon));
99: 
100:     Ok(Edit::deletion(preceding.end(), following.start()))
